Field Notes — Vision Transformers

Teaching a transformer to see, without telling it what to look for.

Three ways of training a Vision Transformer on the same 3,670-image flower herbarium — from raw pixels, from a mask-and-reconstruct pretext task, and from a decade of someone else's labels — compared honestly, on the same held-out plates.

3,670images, 5 species

The question

Where does a transformer's "understanding" of a petal actually come from?

A Vision Transformer has no built-in notion of edges, texture, or locality — the inductive biases a convolutional net gets for free. Everything it knows about images, it has to learn from data. So this project asks a specific question: on a modest, single-domain dataset, what's the cheapest path to a transformer that actually sees something meaningful — and what does that "seeing" look like from the inside?

Regime 01

From scratch

A hand-built ViT — patch embedding, multi-head self-attention, MLP blocks — trained on labels alone, no prior knowledge. The honest baseline for what raw supervision can do on 3,670 images.

Regime 02

Masked autoencoding

The same encoder pretrained with zero labels: mask 75% of each image's patches, reconstruct the missing pixels from what's left. Representation learning by fill-in-the-blank.

Regime 03

ImageNet transfer

A ViT-B/16 pretrained on 1.3M ImageNet images, fine-tuned only on its last two blocks and a fresh head. The ceiling this dataset alone can't reach without borrowed knowledge.

Specimen plates — attention rollout

Where the from-scratch model actually looks

Attention rollout (Abnar & Zuidema, 2020) traces attention weight back through every transformer layer to the input patches — a truer picture than reading a single layer's attention map in isolation. One held-out test image per species, from a 12-epoch proof-of-run on 120 images:

Specimen plate — masked reconstruction

What the pretext task actually reconstructs

75% of this sunflower's patches are hidden from the encoder. The decoder — never told this is a flower, never given a single label — reconstructs the missing regions from petal geometry and color continuity alone.

reconstruction MSE: 1.15 → 0.86 over 10 epochs, 120 unlabeled images, CPU proof-of-run
Embedding atlas

What the encoder's CLS token actually encodes

Every image reduced to its 384-dim CLS embedding after masked-autoencoder pretraining, projected to two dimensions with PCA. No class labels were used to produce these embeddings — only their arrangement is colored by species, after the fact, to check whether the geometry lines up with botany. Reproduce it

Every number and image on this page came from a real, timed run on a single CPU core, saved and embedded as-is — nothing here is a mockup. The full pipeline (all 3,670 images, all three regimes, GPU-ready) lives in train_test_vit_pro.ipynb, with the masked-autoencoder pretraining and attention rollout code in vit_mae.py and attention_rollout.py.
